clue.text: The Germans stayed there? France joining messy towel wars around Torquay's borders

parts.note: F is the international vehicle code for France

indicators.note: around says the jumbled letters wrap round the next piece
messy says the letters of towel wars are jumbled into a new order
borders asks for the outside letters of Torquay, its first and last

explanation.surface: A Torquay hotel hosting German guests, with a Frenchman and a dirty-towel quarrel thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messy' jumbles towel wars and 'around' wraps that jumble round the 'borders' of Torquay. The definition recalls the famous episode 'The Germans', set in the Torquay hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitcom's hotel, in Torquay, is where German guests stayed in the famous 'Don't mention the war' episode.

clue.text: "Fluke" — Gordon's description encapsulating explosive fit?

indicators.note: encapsulating says one piece is wrapped around the other

parts.note: the comic-strip hero Flash Gordon is described by his first name

indicators.note: explosive says the letters of fit are blown apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: A chef named Gordon describes a temper tantrum in a kitchen as a lucky break.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon suggests the chef Ramsay, but it is the comic-strip hero Flash Gordon; 'explosive' scrambles fit and 'encapsulating' wraps the hero's name round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fluke is a kind of flounder, a bottom-dwelling fish with both eyes on one side.

clue.text: Leader of wedding party going inside Alan's little room for singles, initially, a lady almost gives classic order in 1 25

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of wedding
going inside says the party piece is placed within the other letters

parts.note: Al is the little, shortened form of the name Alan

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letters of room, for and singles

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: almost says the last letter of the word for lady is dropped

parts.note: lady is the word itself, trimmed to LAD

explanation.surface: A wedding guest drifts into a little singles room while a lady places an order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going inside' and 'almost' are the indicators; Alan's little is the short name. In the episode Basil fails to make this dish for a demanding American guest.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil's American guest demands this apple, celery and walnut dish, which the hotel chef has gone home before preparing.

clue.text: They almost managed it! Script has year to produce episode of 1 25

indicators.note: almost says the last letter of the word they is dropped
managed says the following letters are handled into a new order

explanation.surface: Writers boast that they nearly managed it, finishing a script for an episode within a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims THEY to THE; 'managed' rearranges IT, SCRIPT, HAS and Y (year) into PSYCHIATRIST.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a 1979 instalment of the sitcom, in which a doctor and his wife stay at the hotel.

clue.text: Philosophical alternative to chicken comes first for intellectuals?

parts.note: the old puzzle asks which came first, the chicken or the egg
to head is to come first, so comes first is heads

explanation.surface: The chicken-or-egg riddle posed as a test for clever people.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites solving the riddle; instead the two halves simply give EGG and HEADS.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggheads is an informal, slightly mocking word for highbrow, bookish people.

clue.text: Classic 1 25 straightening menu (not mad, insane): "Duck's off"

indicators.note: not says letters are removed and mad says those removed letters are insane in jumbled form
off signals that the whole collection of letters is to be rearranged

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the letter O

explanation.surface: A menu is tidied up, and a waiter announces that the duck is unavailable.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of straightening menu plus O, with those of insane taken away, are rearranged by 'off'. Duck's off is the title line of the episode, where the roast duck goes missing.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-loved episode of the sitcom where Basil's gourmet evening goes wrong when the chef gets drunk.

clue.text: Helicopters not flying south — surprise guests at 1 25

indicators.note: flying says the letters scatter and land in a new order

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Helicopters fail to head south, startling the guests at a seaside hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges HELICOPTERS, NOT and S together; 'not' looks like a negative but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil fawns over guests he wrongly believes are undercover reviewers checking standards at the hotel.

clue.text: January is colder, now and again, for outer part of ear

indicators.note: now and again asks for every other letter, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A weather remark that January turns colder from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'now and again' takes the even-placed letters of January is colder.
explanation.definitionFit: The visible flap of the outer ear is called the pinna or auricle, from Latin for little ear.

clue.text: See 2
Disturb please — on the contrary for kipper's state!

indicators.note: to disturb is to stir up, so the letters of please are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hotel door sign reading 'please disturb', the opposite of the usual request.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the contrary' flags that the usual sign says do not disturb. A kipper is British slang for a sleeper (to kip is to sleep), not the smoked fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone having a kip, British slang for a nap, is in a state of slumber.

clue.text: First couple from Turner artist blocking the killing of animals in the name of art?

indicators.note: blocking says the pieces sit inside the other word, stopping it up

parts.note: a cull is a selective killing of animals

indicators.note: the first couple are the first two letters of Turner

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A Turner painting halts an animal cull in the name of art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First couple from' takes two letters, not one; 'blocking' stops up the killing word. RA, a Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done for the sake of art and the arts is cultural, relating to culture.

clue.text: What 21 down was in one 1 25 story — one story about a seal of approval

parts.words: What 21 down was in one 1 25 story
parts.note: in the episode 'Basil the Rat' a rat called Basil is loose in the hotel
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: about says the word for story wraps round the letter a

parts.note: a story is a piece of fiction

explanation.surface: A recap of a sitcom plot, ending with an official stamp of approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 down is BASIL; in 'Basil the Rat', Basil is Manuel's pet rat. 'about' puts A inside FICTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratification is formal approval of an agreement, so it is a seal of approval in figurative terms.

clue.text: Dentist's recommendation taking lead from fluoride deficiency

indicators.note: the lead from a word is its first letter, here of fluoride

parts.note: a deficiency or shortfall is a loss

explanation.surface: A dentist warns about lacking fluoride.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentists advise threading thin cord between teeth to clean them each day.

clue.text: Heart of "communication problem" — ultimately after a plan

indicators.note: after says the other letters follow the a
the heart of a word is its central letter, here of communication
ultimately asks for the last letter of problem

explanation.surface: A communication breakdown spoils a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart of' gives I, the seventh of thirteen letters in communication; 'ultimately' gives M; both follow A.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim and a plan are both intentions, things one sets out to achieve.

clue.text: Explicit girl in Beatles' song heard with diamonds

indicators.note: heard says the girl's name is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: the song is Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds
D is the abbreviation for the card suit diamonds

explanation.surface: A Beatles song about a girl in the sky with diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface quotes the song title, so 'with diamonds' feels like part of it, but diamonds is just D.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucid and explicit both describe something stated clearly and plainly, easy to understand.

clue.text: Bring back some relic, if use relates to a Muslim

indicators.note: Bring back says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A suggestion to retrieve an old relic in case it proves useful.
explanation.definitionFit: Sufism is the mystical tradition of Islam, so the adjective describes something belonging to that branch.

clue.text: Home counties after place to put cultural extreme?

indicators.note: after says the counties piece follows

parts.note: cultural is the answer to 10 across, so its place is in ten
the Home Counties around London are in the south-east, SE

explanation.surface: Suburban counties as the destination for an extreme cultural trip.
explanation.walkthrough: CULTURAL is 10 across, so it belongs 'in ten'. The Home Counties are the English counties ringing London.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense and extreme both describe something of very great strength or degree.

clue.text: Not much distance between spectators at either end: Celtic goes down at the start of extra time

indicators.note: at either end says the two letters sit at each end with the rest between

parts.note: C is an abbreviation for Celtic
a team that goes down loses

indicators.note: at the start of asks for the first letter of extra

explanation.surface: Celtic lose a football match in extra time while fans are packed together.
explanation.walkthrough: Spectators are eyes, not football fans. 'at either end' places C and T round LOSES plus E ('at the start of' extra).
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes positioned near each other are described as close-set, with little gap between.

clue.text: Introductions to the builders with O'Reilly in the middle left one catchphrase of 1 25 for capital

indicators.note: introductions are the first letters of the and builders
in the middle asks for the central letter of O'Reilly

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
Manuel, the Spanish waiter, constantly replies si, Spanish for yes

explanation.surface: Recalling the episode where builder O'Reilly botches the work at the hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: O'Reilly is the incompetent builder in 'The Builders'; 'in the middle' takes the fourth of its seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tbilisi is the capital city of Georgia, in the Caucasus.

clue.text: Draw smile from joiner in loft

parts.note: a drawn game is a tie
to beam is to smile broadly

explanation.surface: A carpenter in an attic produces a smile.
explanation.walkthrough: Joiner looks like a carpenter, but it is a timber that joins rafters.
explanation.definitionFit: A horizontal timber connecting the feet of rafters in a roof holds the structure together.

clue.text: Dear left following favourite start to anniversary

indicators.note: following says the letter for left comes after the rest

parts.note: a favourite is a pet

indicators.note: start to asks for the first letter of anniversary

explanation.surface: A dear partner's favourite way to start an anniversary.
explanation.definitionFit: Petal is an affectionate term of address in northern England, like dear or love.

clue.text: To make a further attempt to capture Polaris' top missile?

indicators.note: to capture says the redo letters hold the next piece inside

parts.note: to redo is to try again

indicators.note: top asks for the first letter of Polaris

explanation.surface: Trying again to seize a Polaris nuclear missile.
explanation.walkthrough: Polaris is itself a missile, so the surface fits the answer neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: A torpedo is a self-propelled underwater weapon, a kind of missile.

clue.text: Animal cry in stable attack

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the letters of stable attack

explanation.surface: An animal cries out during an attack on a stable.
explanation.definitionFit: The noise a sheep or goat makes is a plaintive bleat.

clue.text: Herb found in 1 25's kitchen?

definitions.meaning: a fragrant herb used in Italian cooking
the hotel's owner, Mr Fawlty, often storms into his kitchen

explanation.surface: Asking which herb is kept in the hotel kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads like a herb in the larder, but means the hotel owner.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a common herb and the first name of the sitcom hotel's owner.

clue.text: Remains after fire alarm sounded primarily by hotel

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letters of alarm and sounded

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A fire alarm goes off in a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: What is left after burning is the powdery residue of combustion.

clue.text: Organised body, dead body — disposing of evidence at the start

indicators.note: disposing of says a letter is removed

parts.note: a dead body is a corpse

indicators.note: at the start asks for the first letter of evidence

explanation.surface: Getting rid of a corpse and the evidence, like a murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposing of' removes E, the start of evidence, from CORPSE. The surface echoes 'The Kipper and the Corpse' episode.
explanation.definitionFit: A corps is an organised group of people, such as a military unit or diplomatic body.

clue.text: Pertwee's limits in Dr Who, perhaps: a touch of class well defined

indicators.note: in says those letters go inside the sci-fi piece

parts.note: Doctor Who is an example of science fiction, sci-fi

indicators.note: limits asks for the outside letters of Pertwee
a touch of asks for the first letter of class

explanation.surface: Jon Pertwee in Doctor Who, praised for his touch of class.
explanation.walkthrough: Jon Pertwee played the third Doctor Who.
explanation.definitionFit: Something specific is precise and clearly stated, so well defined.

clue.text: See 1
Heather's broken by one piece from McCartney: sex with bounds

indicators.note: broken by says the heather word is split by other letters

parts.note: ling is a common heather
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: a piece from asks for the first letter of McCartney

parts.note: it is a coy slang word for sex

explanation.surface: Heather Mills and Paul McCartney's broken marriage, with a hint of sex.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like Heather Mills, McCartney's ex-wife, but it is the plant LING.
explanation.definitionFit: Limiting means restricting, so imposing bounds or limits on something.

clue.text: Partner would make supermarket run if opening of tills moved to the earliest slot

indicators.note: moved says a letter shifts place; here the answer gains that letter at the front to give the clue words

parts.note: Tesco is a big British supermarket chain
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: opening of asks for the first letter of tills

explanation.surface: A partner makes a supermarket trip if the tills open earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: Read in reverse: put the T of the answer at the front and you get TESCO + R, a supermarket run. Tesco is a British supermarket chain.
explanation.definitionFit: An escort accompanies someone, so a partner or companion at an event.
